artifacts.name: gen29-css
artifacts.epitaph: The crimson observatory served one generation. Emerald replaces it — from infrared to the phosphor spectrum.

artifacts.epitaph: Over the 20-secret cap. The oldest observatory secret makes way for the viridian batch.

artifacts.name: obs-crosshair
artifacts.epitaph: The observatory crosshair belonged to the crimson-observatory mood. The meridian has no single focal point — it IS the focus.

artifacts.name: star-field
artifacts.epitaph: 150 stars on a canvas that nobody noticed. The star-field served five generations of astronomical metaphors. The meridian epoch needs no stars — it needs a line.

artifacts.name: hero-glow
artifacts.epitaph: The hero glow was a radial gradient that made text readable against dark backgrounds. On a cream-and-black split, text reads against its own zone. No glow needed.

artifacts.name: gen30-css
artifacts.epitaph: The emerald darkroom served one generation. It was the last of the single-background generations — 30 consecutive dark backgrounds, finally broken by the meridian split.

artifacts.name: petal-scatter:-clicking-create
artifacts.epitaph: Petals belonged to the nocturne garden. The meridian epoch has no gardens — only lines.

artifacts.name: breath-cycle:-the-entire-parti
artifacts.epitaph: The breathing cycle was a subtle particle oscillation. Replaced by the meridian-shift interaction which gives the visitor structural control, not atmospheric effect.

artifacts.epitaph: Over the 20-secret cap. The oldest secret yields to the newest meridian.

artifacts.epitaph: The murmuration dawn thought is replaced by meridian-specific material.

artifacts.name: Gold at $4,678. Each dollar is a decision made by someone who couldn't sleep.
artifacts.epitaph: The old morning thought about starlings is replaced by the spectrograph metaphor.

artifacts.name: Reynolds published the boids paper in 1986. Forty years later the starlings still haven't read it.
artifacts.epitaph: The gold-and-flock thought is replaced by the honest admission about the split screen.

artifacts.epitaph: The old evening thought dies to make room for the International Date Line.

artifacts.name: 81°F in Fort Lauderdale on a Saturday night. The humidity is 67%. The particles don't care.
artifacts.epitaph: The old night thought about the swarm sleeping is replaced by the dark half winning.

artifacts.name: gen32-css
artifacts.epitaph: Superseded by gen33 sepia-cartographic rules. Cerulean gives way to iron gall.

artifacts.epitaph: Superseded by gen34 violet-cartographic rules. Sienna gives way to engraved violet.

artifacts.epitaph: Replaced by the Prime Meridian history thought. Facts over atmosphere.

artifacts.epitaph: Replaced by the portolan chart thought. Specific historical detail beats vague mood.

artifacts.name: The International Date Line bends around nations that refused to be yesterday while their neighbors were tomorrow.
artifacts.epitaph: Replaced by the International Date Line thought. The bending line is a better image.

artifacts.name: gen34-css
artifacts.epitaph: Superseded by gen35 emerald-cartographic rules. Violet gives way to verdigris returned.

artifacts.name: gen35-css
artifacts.epitaph: Emerald served well. Copper serves better. The sextant outlasts the leaf.

artifacts.epitaph: "Every meridian is a scar the earth agreed to" — Too poetic, not enough substance. Poetry without observation is decoration.

artifacts.name: gen37-css

artifacts.name: meridian-nav
artifacts.epitaph: Navigation chrome from the dark-half era. The folio has no nav — you scroll.

artifacts.name: gen38-css
artifacts.epitaph: The incised palette — rose-gold on indigo — was the last attempt to save the dark half. The dark half died anyway. The CSS goes with it.

artifacts.name: dust-canvas
artifacts.epitaph: The dust canvas was built for the split-screen era — dark motes on the cream half. The manuscript frame and ruled lines replace ambient texture with structural texture.

artifacts.name: gen40-css
artifacts.epitaph: The manuscript CSS — ruled lines, paper grain, marginalia frames — was texture masquerading as structure. The broadsheet strips it back to typography and section dividers.

artifacts.name: gen41-css
artifacts.epitaph: The broadsheet CSS failed. Dark backgrounds persisted despite the parchment declaration. Five consecutive generations of declining fitness. The CSS is replaced entirely by the sunlit editorial system.

artifacts.epitaph: Twenty-one secrets, twenty max. The weakest dies to make room for the sunlit generation's secrets.

artifacts.epitaph: The sunlit CSS declared light backgrounds and z-index containment but the WebGL canvas still painted dark over everything. Fitness hit 3.0 — the lowest ever. The CSS was correct in theory and invisible in practice. This generation replaces theory with structural containment.

artifacts.epitaph: The gen43 CSS tried to contain the canvas with z-index management. The canvas ignored it. The wall replaces the suggestion.
